coverage.finding: Folio number '322' with superscript 'b' and a dot-like mark before the 'b'. It is in the top-left margin, about [460,365,170,145]. A faint grey smudge just above it looks like an erasure or stain. No legible text could be read in it.

One line runs from the left margin across the main column, with a left-pointing arrow near the right page edge, about x 2945–3100, y 950. The cursive middle words ('most misleadingly damaged') stay tentative. The sign in 'first + last' and the one in '6 & 84' look alike, so the use of '+' in one place and '&' in the other is not secure. The candidate already flags this.
Line and arrow confirmed. The blotted or overwritten letter after 'prakāś' is visible. The letter read as 'n.' in '(n. 38ff.)' could also be 'm.'; the reading is retained as uncertain.
Broken horizontal rule below b003, in two dash segments. It contains no text.

Line and arrow confirmed, arrow at about x 3004–3129, y 3168. 'S.1942' shows a plain S, and the following word looks like 'Sake'. No acute is clearly visible over the S. The candidate's literal 'Śaka' asserts more than the source shows. A mark like a diaeresis sits above the final i of 'Hemādri'. 'I.O.' is written with dots and looks like '1.0.'.
Indented line 'ff.9-42. I.O.3533' with an arrow at about x 2989–3114, y 3290, aligned with d.305(4) on the facing page.

Centred cross-reference. After 'Hari' there are separated strokes like 'm', then a free-standing 'ī', then 'ḍ' with a dot below. The candidate's '[mī?]' uncertainty is appropriate. The writing is consistent with c.224(9) on the facing page, but that page is also hard to read.

Two-line note in a smaller hand at about [2324,4016,700,115]. There is no arrow on this page. On the facing page, a short right-pointing arrow sits under 'b.42(2)' at the same height. The attachment is plausible but not secure. The note's closeness to b007 is spatial only.

review.boundary_review: The target page ends at about x 3135. The facing page fol. 323 begins beyond the gutter, and its left-margin shelfmarks (c.280 through b.100) are context only.
